name: Bokeh Naturalness
description: Evaluates depth-of-field blur disc shapes and optical aberration patterns against real lens models to identify computationally simulated bokeh lacking authentic optical imperfections.
mechanism:
This method analyzes bokeh (out-of-focus rendering) naturalness for forensic detection:

1. **Depth-of-Field Map Estimation**: The image is analyzed to estimate relative depth across the frame using defocus cues. Regions are classified by their blur level — sharp (in-focus), slightly blurred, and heavily blurred, creating a depth-ordered defocus map.

2. **Bokeh Disc Analysis**: Out-of-focus highlights are identified and their shape (bokeh disc) is analyzed. Real lenses produce bokeh discs with shapes determined by the aperture blade count and shape — circular, hexagonal, or octagonal with consistent geometry across the frame. AI-generated bokeh often produces physically impossible disc shapes or inconsistent shapes at different frame positions.

3. **Defocus Gradient Consistency**: The transition from sharp to blurred regions should follow a smooth gradient consistent with optical depth-of-field physics (proportional to 1/distance from focal plane). AI generators may produce abrupt focus transitions, incorrect blur gradient directions, or depth-of-field effects inconsistent with any physical lens.

4. **Chromatic Aberration in Bokeh**: Real out-of-focus regions exhibit longitudinal chromatic aberration — color fringing with green/magenta shifts depending on whether the object is in front of or behind the focal plane. The method checks for correct chromatic behavior in bokeh regions. Generated images typically lack or incorrectly render chromatic bokeh effects.

5. **Temporal Bokeh Consistency**: In video, bokeh characteristics should vary smoothly with camera-to-subject distance changes. The method tracks bokeh quality across frames — generated video may produce inconsistent frame-to-frame bokeh rendering, with disc shapes, blur amounts, or chromatic effects that fluctuate without corresponding depth changes.
parameters:
Analysis type: sensor
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through bokeh naturalness analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
